Sumter County public housing inventory remains at 326 units in 2025
Sumter County recorded 326 public housing units in 2025, unchanged from 2024.
Sumter County reported 326 public housing units in 2025, the same number as in 2024, according to HUD's Picture of Subsidized Households.
Housing Choice Voucher assistance covered 917 voucher units.
Sumter County had 519 project-based units, including Project Based Section 8, 202/PRAC and 811/PRAC.
The occupancy rate for public housing units in Sumter County was 97%, with 10 units vacant.
Residents of Sumter County public housing paid 376 per month in rent, equal to 29% of income.
Among Sumter County public housing residents, 2% were Hispanic, 95% were minority, 92% were Black non-Hispanic, 5% were white non-Hispanic and 2% were Native American non-Hispanic.
Sumter County ranked 10th among South Carolina's 37 counties, placing it among the state's top 10 counties.
HUD-assisted housing programs generally lower rent for eligible low-income households. HUD's Picture of Subsidized Households outlines three broad assistance categories: public housing, tenant-based assistance and privately owned, project-based assistance. Local housing agencies own public housing, while tenant-based assistance, including housing vouchers, helps households rent homes in the private market. Project-based assistance applies to specific privately owned properties covered by HUD rental-assistance contracts.
Households receiving HUD rental assistance generally pay rent equal to 30% of income after deductions, and the federal government covers the remaining rent or rental costs. Eligibility is based on HUD income limits, which vary by location and household size; applicants are typically placed on a waiting list until assistance is available.
